A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HopaDIFF and RHAS133. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original RHAS133 benchmark experiments, component ablations, and an appendix experiment varying frame length.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds controlled comparisons, efficiency measurements, further ablations, and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The proposed dual-branch diffusion framework, GroundingDINO crops, HP-xLSTM, Fourier conditioning, losses, and output averaging remain unchanged. Appendix B further specifies the existing BCA mechanism; experimental variants do not replace the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same RHAS133 referring action segmentation task, with 133 movies, 542 individuals, and 137 action classes. Random and cross-movie coverage remains unchanged. Cropped-input controls and rare-class discussion concern existing data, not additional task or population coverage.

E2.justification: The five primary benchmark baselines remain unchanged. V2 expands Table 5 with FACT using a partial branch, ActDIFF with Fourier conditioning, and a Cross-Attention Fusion comparator citing CrossViT.

E3.justification: V2 adds controlled cropped-input evaluations, alternative component configurations, and parameter-count, inference-time, and GFLOPS measurements. Existing split sizes, clip lengths, backbones, training settings, and ACC/EDIT/F1 metrics remain unchanged. The statement that features are pre-extracted clarifies implementation rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends the diagnostic evidence with component-transfer and fusion controls, cropped-input baseline comparisons, merged versus dual heads, removal of diffusion, and qualitative/error analysis (Tables 5–6 and 9–11; Figure 5). The original frame-length study is retained as Table 8. Table 11 partly redisplays existing branch-removal results rather than constituting wholly new evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4, the original Table 5 rows, and the frame-length results remain numerically unchanged. V2 adds substantial ablation, efficiency, and qualitative results; for example, Table 9 reports test ACC of 56.50 for merged heads versus 59.63 for the full model. New tables also contain conflicting repeated values: full-model test F1@10 is 90.11 in Tables 6 and 9–11 but remains 90.91 in Tables 3 and 5. This does not establish a performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds explicit mathematical definitions of BCA attention weights and cross-attended gate inputs in Equations 8–11, whereas v1 only names the operator in Equation 5. This is a limited extension of the mathematical specification; the original equations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the RHAS task, RHAS133 dataset and benchmark, and HopaDIFF with HP-xLSTM and Fourier conditioning. The new contribution-summary paragraph restates these existing claims, and the asserted state-of-the-art scope remains RHAS133.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of periodic frequency patterns, complementary contextual and cropped cues, and the dual-head accuracy/F1 versus EDIT tradeoff. It newly acknowledges inference-efficiency limitations of the two-stage pipeline and rare-class confusion. The single-dataset limitation remains in the appendix despite its removal from the conclusion.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents pre-extracted VLM features and baseline input conventions, expands BCA specification, and reports model sizes and computational costs in Table 7. Its abstract now advertises dataset access alongside code. Existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are retained; the PDFs do not establish changed underlying implementations or independently verify resource availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to CrossViT, ObjectRelator, embodied one-shot video recognition, and spatial-relations few-shot action recognition. CrossViT supports the added fusion comparison. The broader positioning against referring recognition and conventional action segmentation remains unchanged; publication updates to existing references are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: V2 adds an explicit contribution summary and explanatory appendix sections, with limited wording, affiliation, acknowledgment, and conference-header edits. Most existing prose and the main section order are retained, so the revision is an expansion rather than an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation expands substantially: Table 5 gains grouped controls, Tables 6, 7, and 9–11 add comparison displays, and Figure 5 introduces a qualitative timeline. Existing tables are relocated or renumbered, including the frame-length table becoming Table 8. The original person-count plot is retained as Figure 4 and duplicated as Figure 6.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the unchanged design easier to assess through cropped-input and alternative-fusion controls, dual-head/diffusion ablations, efficiency measurements, and specific limitations. These address gaps in v1's experimental support. The benefit is tempered by new reporting inconsistencies, including 90.11 versus 90.91 for full-model test F1@10 and 3.26 versus 2.36 for ActDIFF test ACC, while uncertainty estimates remain absent.
